dossier.architecture: Fixed-angle cascading elevator, rigid arm and wristed floor-acquisition gripper.

subsystems.intake: Narrower gripper chosen to fit between hybrid-node dividers and retrieve/rescore pieces; team primarily uses human-player floor loading.
subsystems.transfer: Direct acquisition; no separate transfer described.
subsystems.scoring: Wide two-stage cascading elevator tilted to match cone-node geometry; wrist supplies end-effector orientation.
subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; module model is not specified in the interview.
subsystems.endgame: Dashboard checks pitch/roll for autonomous engage; detailed endgame mechanics not specified.
subsystems.controls: Game-piece state is remembered from operator selection, not automatically detected. Custom dashboard and clothoid-path tooling support operation.

versions: Wrist transmission changed from belts to chain for load handling.
Torque-carrying structure changed from half-inch hex to REV MAXSpline tubing.
dossier.analysis: The narrow intake is an intentional scoring-access tradeoff, not automatically an inferior collector. This is a good test case for an agent that otherwise assumes full width is always better.

context_documents.body:
# 2023-2468: A narrower claw purchases access to contested low geometry

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A narrow gripper handles both pieces, with a wide tilted cascading elevator and wrist. Cross-bracing resists parallelogram deformation; shimmed gearing and a chain wrist reduce play under the collector load.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The retained account ties claw width to fitting between hybrid dividers for retrieval/re-scoring. The team says a chain held the wrist load better than its belt trial.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Maximum acquisition width is not always optimal. A smaller receiver can access a task a wider collector cannot, provided pickup tolerance remains acceptable. Elevator tilt can improve approach geometry while changing tip margin and wrist loads.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure pickup tolerance, low-node retrieval clearance, wrist hysteresis and full-extension stability.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.
